image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) lying on dark, wet sand mixed with small shell fragments. The crab is oriented vertically with its head towards the top. The carapace is broad and oval, exhibiting a mottled pattern of beige, tan, and light brown with darker speckles. The ventral side (underside) is partially visible due to the angle, showing cream-colored segments. Two large, robust claws (chelipeds) are prominent at the front, with dark tips and serrated inner edges visible. Multiple walking legs extend laterally from the body, appearing segmented and jointed. The texture appears hard and calcified, consistent with a crustacean exoskeleton.
